title: Negative: a membrane that gates the autocatalyst's hops (Ono-Ikegami-like) only slightly refines the lattice-chem A pattern (wavelength 11.7 vs 12.9 px), and a ringless twin with uniformly slower A does more (9.0 px); no discrete cells at the weak-repulsion point
summary: Follow-up to 20261025T1656-c19-lattice-chem-ring-passive, which found the energetic M ring passive. world.py here adds a hop gate: an A hop across a face is suppressed by exp(-gA (M_here + M_target)/n0), so membrane holds the autocatalyst while food passes freely. To give the wall a job I weakened the A-W repulsion (phi_AW 0.5 instead of 1.5), where A alone coarsens into large domains, and ran three arms on seeds 0 and 1 (128^2, 10000 steps; run_arms.sh): gate (gA 3), no gate, and the slow-diffusion twin (no gate, A hop rate pA 0.06 instead of 0.2 everywhere). The gate thickens the M layer (labkit M rim/core 1.59-1.60 vs 1.10-1.14 without) and refines the A pattern: structure-factor wavelength 11.5/11.9 px vs 12.9/12.8 px (domain.txt; sheets: compartmented labyrinth vs coarse A patches). The slow-A twin, with no functional wall, refines it further, to 9.0/9.0 px (slowA/seed0/sheet.png), and its M ring is sharper too (rim/core 2.27-2.32). Bath A is not lower with the gate (0.46-0.50 vs 0.43; ringwork.txt). At this point A forms a connected labyrinth, not discrete cells, in all three arms. So a hop-gating membrane does some work here, but less than uniformly slower transport: the same lesson as the FCH shells and c15's fuel ring.

finding.operator: membrane hop gate exp(-gA (M_i + M_j)/n0) on the autocatalyst in a lattice artificial chemistry
finding.control: matched no-gate arm and slow-A twin (pA 0.06 everywhere, no gate), same seeds 0 and 1, grid, duration, phi_AW 0.5

limits: One gate strength (gA 3) and one repulsion point (phi_AW 0.5), 2 seeds, 10000 steps; the wavelength metric uses the mean k of S(k) over the lower half of the spectrum and is sensitive to lattice noise, so read it as an ordering, which the sheets confirm; at phi_AW 0.5 there are no discrete individuals, so this tests compartmentation, not cells. To stay small, seed 1 keeps only FACTS.md and metrics.json.
